key_insight: OrganLens learns organ-specific CT representations from a shared encoder, using organ identity and self-supervision to produce 11 organ-focused features without requiring segmentation masks at inference.
clinical_relevance: This could improve organ-targeted imaging research by making CT foundation models more sensitive to disease signals tied to a specific organ while still preserving useful whole-volume context.
method: Shared CT encoder is conditioned on organ identity before features are formed.
Anatomy-mask supervision and organ-specific distillation guide anatomy-weighted pooling into organ representations.
At inference, the model outputs 11 organ-specific embeddings from the same CT scan without external masks.
evidence_signal: Evaluated on CT-RATE, RAD-ChestCT, INSPECT, and NLST, OrganLens improved organ-relevant downstream performance, including cardiomegaly AUROC rising from 0.910 to 0.953 and lung-cancer mortality C-index improving by 14.2%.
watch_item: Performance gains may depend on reliable organ conditioning and the training anatomy mix, so generalization to uncommon scanners, pathologies, or missing organ coverage still needs validation.
paper_title: OrganLens: Organ-Specific Representation Learning for CT Foundation Models
